key_insight: Router-ahead prefetch hides tier latency only when few experts are hot. It suits small-batch or edge MoE serving from trailing-node DDR4.
killer_doubt: At batch >=64 nearly every expert fires each layer. DeepSeek-V3 needs ~350 MB per layer in ~0.5 ms (~700 GB/s); CXL x16 gives ~64 GB/s, so misses stall.
decisive_experiment: Replay DeepSeek-V3 and Mixtral router traces at batch 1-256 through a CXL-DDR4 latency and bandwidth model. Measure the per-layer union of experts and the stall fraction. Software only, ~$20k.
prior_art: Pre-gated MoE (ISCA 2024), MoE-Infinity, ProMoE, Fiddler, HOBBIT, MoE-Lightning; DDR4 reuse behind CXL (Microsoft GreenSKU) (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Packing sub-line words saves link bytes for truly sparse 4-8 B gathers, and the base-die command path is the right place to do it.
killer_doubt: Each word still opens a 1-2 KB page, so activation and on-die movement (~2/3 of ~3.5 pJ/bit) stay. Embedding rows are 128-512 B, so most traffic gains <=1.3x.
decisive_experiment: Run a trace-driven Ramulator2 study of DLRM, SpMV and paged-KV gathers with packed returns. Report link bytes and total pJ per useful bit. Software, ~$30k.
prior_art: Impulse memory controller (Utah 1999), GS-DRAM (MICRO 2015), TensorDIMM (MICRO 2019), RecNMP (ISCA 2020), Samsung AxDIMM (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Top-k selection can sit next to the KV store. Returning only the selected keys and values at full precision cuts link energy in long-context decode.
killer_doubt: HBM TSV bandwidth roughly equals PHY bandwidth (~1-2 TB/s per stack), so the base die still streams every key. Storage is unchanged; SparQ/Quest save the same on GPU.
decisive_experiment: Measure top-k recall and accuracy against k with 4-bit key scoring on RULER and LongBench. Model base-die versus GPU-side selection energy using HBM4 TSV counts. Software, ~$50k.
prior_art: AttAcc (ASPLOS 2024), NeuPIMs, SK hynix AiM; Quest (ICML 2024), SparQ, InfiniGen (OSDI 2024) do query-aware top-k KV fetch (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Read-only weights need one copy. A passive splitter tree amortizes the transmitter, and a central node can hold weights in cheap LPDDR instead of N copies in HBM.
killer_doubt: Each receiver needs the full weight-read rate: 70 GB per 30 ms is ~19 Tb/s, ~$1.9k at $0.1/Gbps, versus ~$1.0-1.75k HBM saved. 1:128 split loses 21 dB.
decisive_experiment: Build a 1:32 PLC splitter testbed fed by a 16-wavelength x 100G DWDM source and an EDFA booster. Measure BER and power margin at every port. Add a cost model for 10-20 Tb/s receive-only SiPh chiplets. ~$400k.
prior_art: Cerebras weight streaming (MemoryX/SwarmX broadcast, electrical); Celestial AI photonic memory fabric (prior knowledge). Passive optical weight broadcast to accelerators: none found.

key_insight: Same insight as I-05406 at 1:16: one weight read can be broadcast to every data-parallel replica through mass-produced passive splitters.
killer_doubt: PON optics run 10-50 Gb/s (<=6 GB/s) per port against ~2 TB/s of weight reads per accelerator, ~300x short. Moving to DWDM fixes bandwidth but turns this into I-05406.
decisive_experiment: No separate experiment. I-05406's DWDM splitter testbed and receiver cost model settle this one, because telecom PON line rates are fixed.
prior_art: Same as I-05406; telecom XGS-PON and 50G-PON splitter trees (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Area cost is the lever: at ~0.05 um2/bit (~50x below DRAM density), IGZO gain cells on glass under $1,000/m2 cost ~$0.9/GB, below DDR5, with negligible refresh.
killer_doubt: At 45 nm, patterning cost scales with area on any substrate: ~8 critical layers at ~$500-900/m2 is ~$5k/m2 (~$4/GB). Glass compaction (~5-20 ppm) defeats ~10 nm overlay.
decisive_experiment: On 150 mm glass coupons, use HP-style self-aligned multilevel imprint (SAIL) to make a 64-kb IGZO 2T0C array at 50-100 nm, which needs no overlay. Measure yield, Vt sigma, 85 C retention and compaction maps. ~$600k.
prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO NOSRAM/DOSRAM (on Si); HP SAIL roll-to-roll TFTs; PragmatIC flexible IGZO ICs; NIL wire-grid polarizers on panels (prior knowledge). Panel-scale DRAM: none found.

key_insight: Synchronized twin predictors with 1-bit hit flags are a clean lossless link code for pointer-, stride- and zero-rich traffic at a CXL controller or HBM base die.
killer_doubt: bf16 and fp8 weights and activations are nearly incompressible (entropy ~0.8-0.95 of raw), and measured link compression is 1.2-2x on general code. A CRC replay desynchronizes both predictors.
decisive_experiment: Capture memory-link traces from SPEC, graph and LLM workloads. Simulate stride, context and value twin predictors, and report bits per 64 B line and added latency. Software, ~$20k.
prior_art: T0 bus encoding (Benini 1997); Thuresson-Stenstrom value-locality memory-link compression (IEEE TC 2008); frequent-value encoding; GPU lossless bandwidth compression (prior knowledge).

key_insight: The kT/C arithmetic holds (~0.2 mV rms on 100 fF), but it is not the floor. Offset and coupled noise are, and trimmed clocked latches can work at ~20-50 mV.
killer_doubt: PHY plus interposer is only ~0.5-1 of HBM's 3-4 pJ/bit; UCIe-A already reaches ~0.25-0.5 and hybrid bonds ~0.05, so stack gain <=20%. ~10-30 mV switching noise eats margin.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a 28 nm MPW test chip with a 64-lane, 5 mm interposer-class link: charge-dump TX and trimmed StrongARM RX at 20, 50 and 100 mV. Measure BER against aggressor crosstalk, and fJ/bit. ~$300k.
prior_art: Ho/Horowitz capacitively driven low-swing wires (JSSC 2008); NVIDIA ground-referenced signaling (~0.54 pJ/bit); UCIe-A and BoW D2D PHYs (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Bit-plane placement lets low-significance planes tolerate ~1% BER, so binned-out or weak dies could hold LSB planes and add usable supply.
killer_doubt: Savings are small: on-die ECC is ~6% of bits, refresh 16-33% of idle power. Plane-splitting confines MSB-only fetches to 4 of 12 dies, a third of stack bandwidth.
decisive_experiment: Inject 1e-3 to 1e-2 BER into the low mantissa planes of bf16 and fp8 Llama-class weights and measure perplexity. Add a census of die-sort rejects that would pass at 1% BER. ~$50k.
prior_art: Sparkk (MEMSYS 2014) MSB/LSB refresh split; Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); EDEN (MICRO 2019); Any-Precision LLM bit-plane layout (ICML 2024) (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Retention is set by the workload: data re-read every 100 us tolerates 640x leakier cells, which removes the high-aspect-ratio capacitor requirement.
killer_doubt: Mature-node planar eDRAM is ~0.04-0.15 um2/bit versus ~0.001 um2 for DRAM (40-150x). Wafers ~3x cheaper leave $/bit 13-50x worse; 100 us revolutions aren't DRAM-class access.
decisive_experiment: Paper cost model only: published 28 nm eDRAM bitcell areas times depreciated wafer price, against DDR5 $/GB. Revisit only if a mature-node cell <=0.01 um2 appears. ~$10k.
prior_art: Delay-line and drum memories (1950s); logic eDRAM and gain-cell eDRAM (IBM deep-trench, Intel 22 nm eDRAM) (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Per-mat bonded ports remove the intra-die global data bus (~1/3 of access energy) and periphery from the array wafer. SeDRAM ships the bank-level version, proving the physics.
killer_doubt: DRAM over hot logic at 95-105 C has ~4x tail leakage, pulling refresh to ~16 ms. Each die needs 3M+ bonds at <=1 um pitch, demanding mat-level redundancy.
decisive_experiment: Die-to-wafer hybrid-bond (imec/Leti) a 28 nm logic MPW with per-mat ports to a short-bitline or BEOL-IGZO array. Measure pJ/bit per mat against SeDRAM's 0.88, bond yield, and retention at 105 C. ~$800k.
prior_art: UniIC/XMC SeDRAM: IEDM 2020, 34 GB/s/Gb, 0.88 pJ/b, mass-produced (via search snippet). Samsung periphery-under-cell 4F2 VCT (2028); Kioxia CBA; YMTC Xtacking.

key_insight: Lithographic vias over transfer-printed thin dies could give hybrid-bond-class 2-3 um pitch without HB tools, CMP flatness or particle-free bonding: a capital-light U.S. path.
killer_doubt: Transfer-print placement is ~+/-1.5 um (3 sigma), too coarse for 2-3 um pitch without per-die adaptive litho. DRAM thinned below 10 um loses gettering, which may shift the retention tail.
decisive_experiment: Grind DRAM test dies to 8-10 um, transfer-print them onto a logic wafer, planarize with BCB, and align 2.5 um vias die by die on a stepper. Measure via-chain yield (1e5), placement error, and retention before and after. ~$350k.
prior_art: X-Celeprint/X Display micro-transfer printing of CMOS chiplets (Rogers lineage); chip-first fan-out with Deca adaptive patterning; Fraunhofer chip-in-polymer (prior knowledge).
